comments.explanation: SHIFT-001 records 59 nonconforming units out of 500 inspected (rate 0.118), which lies above the upper clipped three-sigma control limit of approximately 0.03538 for its sample size, so it is flagged as a higher-direction signal. This is a comparison against control limits derived from the frozen baseline (BASE-001 through BASE-020, p-bar about 0.01769), not against an acceptance specification, and it indicates process variation only.

SHIFT-002 records 72 nonconforming units out of 800 inspected (rate 0.09), exceeding the upper control limit of approximately 0.03168 for that sample size, yielding a higher-direction signal. The comparison assumes independent, comparable inspections under the same site, product, process, method and regime as the reviewer-accepted stable baseline; control limits are not acceptance specifications.

SHIFT-003 records 43 nonconforming units out of 500 inspected (rate 0.086), above the upper control limit of approximately 0.03538 for its sample size, so it is a higher-direction signal relative to the frozen baseline. The observation describes only the measured rate versus control limits and does not address acceptance specifications or any causal attribution.

SHIFT-004 records 81 nonconforming units out of 800 inspected (rate 0.10125), above the upper control limit of approximately 0.03168 for that sample size, producing a higher-direction signal. Under the stated assumption of independent and comparable inspections against the frozen baseline, this reflects statistical variation beyond three-sigma control limits, which are distinct from acceptance specifications.

SHIFT-005 records 46 nonconforming units out of 500 inspected (rate 0.092), above the upper control limit of approximately 0.03538 for its sample size, giving a higher-direction signal. The finding is a comparison of the observed rate to control limits computed from the frozen baseline (BASE-001 through BASE-020) and is not a comparison to acceptance specifications.
